_meta.protocol: sampled-100 leave-one-out, 5295 test users, K in {5,10,20}

key_findings.improvement_b_done_right: M3b (real heterogeneous graph + edge-dropout two-view InfoNCE) HR@10=0.4072 vs M3 (feature-dropout approx) 0.4043. Gain +0.003 — marginal. Improvement B implemented per paper but data limits the gain.
key_findings.usercf_dominates: UserCF (0.5022) beats ALL learned models including ours (0.4072) and LightGCN (0.4149). Root cause: synthetic interactions are popularity-weighted, so user-user cosine similarity captures the popularity pattern directly. This is a property of the synthetic data, not UserCF's intrinsic strength.
key_findings.data_is_ceiling: All learned models cluster at HR@10 0.40-0.41 (M0/M3/M3b/LightGCN), while non-learned popularity/UserCF exploit the synthetic-data popularity bias better. The complex KG+GAT+contrastive machinery learns nothing beyond popularity on this data.
key_findings.cold_start_contradiction: Cold-item HR@10=0.0185 (near-random) confirms BPR-MF family cannot handle uninteracted items, yet UserCF thrives — again pointing to popularity bias as the dominant learnable signal.

vs_paper.root_cause: synthetic data lacks genuine collaborative structure (1509 real + 39097 popularity-weighted synthetic interactions)

honest_assessment: Per EXPERIMENT_PLAN principle '真实可复现的 0.48 > 编造的 0.561'. The 0.561 target is unreachable on this synthetic data regardless of model complexity — UserCF at 0.5022 is likely near the data's ceiling. Recommend: (1) report real numbers honestly, (2) stage 3 tuning/seed-repeats unlikely to close 0.15 gap, (3) paper revision should reflect Amazon synthetic-data caveat.
